sourceCurriculum.sourceNotes: The selected 2026–2027 pathway totals 180 EC: ten 6 EC compulsory units in Year 1; ten 6 EC Year-2 units, retaining all three part-II subjects; and 30 EC open study, three 6 EC restricted electives and a 12 EC thesis in Year 3. The selected electives are Econometrics III, Mathematical Economics III and Financial Econometrics; they are choices, not requirements for every student. The thesis follows the Econometrics specialisation. Open study remains subject to level, approval and entry conditions. Mandatory zero-credit study-support and English-language requirements sit outside the 180 EC. This is one valid pathway, not every possible combination. Year 1 is 60 EC. Its annual guide lists BRIDGE, SAM Programme EOR/EDS and the English Language Test at 0 EC; the narrative explicitly requires a full-year zero-credit course and the diagnostic. They are recorded separately, without interpreting their coexistence as extra credits. A failed English diagnostic requires the refresher; the introductory EOR grade requires the language condition. BSA normally requires 42 first-year EC and a pass in at least one calculus/analysis course AND at least one Probability Theory/Statistics course, subject to the regulations. Year 2 is 60 EC: seven compulsory units and the three prescribed part-II units retained here; one part-II may be replaced only with prior programme-director permission. Integrative Practical requires a partial mark of at least 5.5 in at least one of Econometrics I/Mathematical Economics I/Operations Research I. Advanced Practical requires a pass from each group: Statistics/Probability Theory(EOR)/Introduction to Data Science(EDS); Programming/Numerical Methods; and Econometrics I/Mathematical Economics I/Operations Research I. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including the relevant part-II course; Econometrics II is retained for this Econometrics thesis. The thesis is independent academic research with a paper and uploaded/presented poster, supervisor and second-reader assessment; register for Canvas and use Onstage. Submission before 1 July and approval before 1 August are needed for the stated pre-September graduation process, not extra EC. Tutorial/practical attendance may be required under individual manuals. Open Year-3 study is 30 EC: at most 6 EC at level 100, at least 12 EC at level 300, normally 90 EC for minor entry; prior board approval is required except stated faculty/university/Education-minor exemptions. The Economics university minor is unavailable to EOR students. Exchange, internships and individual packages need their applicable permissions. Honours and transitional arrangements are not stacked into this pathway. Material source reconciliation: the guide elective narrative says choose one or two of nine broader electives; the adopted OER Appendix VII annual chart says at most two. The selected Financial Econometrics plus two Ect/OR/ME-III subjects satisfies both, without relying on the disputed zero-other-elective interpretation. Financial Econometrics follows Econometrics III in P5; the other two are P4. This retains the neutral Econometrics route and a breadth subject from mathematical economics, adding the degree’s evidenced financial application; the choice is unrelated to UCR fit. The annual chart visibly calls E_EOR3_TR3 Econometrics II, but its code and the current guide/Pure course establish Econometrics III. Visible year and version 26-2-2026 agree; no older hidden edition was used.

allSelectedCourses.contentReview: All actual enriched profiles, methods/topics, prerequisites and offerings read. Each course’s bounded contribution is in repaired trace and associated profile evidence. Accounting/Linear Systems/AI planning overclaims corrected.

comparability: Retain qualified positive comparison: substantial mathematics/statistics/computing/economic and optimisation content responds to the degree, with one actual econometrics course. Explicitly missing advanced econometric/time-series/financial-risk, stochastic-OR and network/game-theoretic progression; adjacent signals/accounting are not substitutes. Primary is methods/economic inquiry; second adds a distinct 60-EC application-domain change.

candidateAssessment.assessment: All 36 linked rows were checked against current official evidence. Twelve are generator-eligible: the primary owns six core quantitative/economic/programming/econometrics and shock-analysis interests (4326,4327,4330,4332–4334), with limited specialist-finance coverage stated. The two energy/production interests (4329,4331) generate the second composition with eight substantive substitutions, 60 EC exclusive on each side. OR/capacity planning (4328,4335) cannot justify a distinct third programme: existing algorithms, AI optimisation/planning and numerical methods already supply its available UCR response, without dedicated hospital planning or stochastic-OR depth. Mathematical Economics (4336) fails specialist feasibility: UCR does contain game-theory and general-equilibrium topics in economics, but lacks the dedicated mathematical-economics progression, network games and empirical-network methods. Networks (4337) similarly cannot be supplied by computer-network or graph-search courses. Rows 4338–4348 support curricular assessment; 4349–4351 are examples and 4352–4361 are career/further-study outcomes, not independent programme generators. The current homepage replaces the historical Brexit/interbank-loan example with bank impacts of an interest-rate shock; no continuing specific Brexit or interbank-loan teaching is promised. Current future pages substantiate the broader professions/applications. Stop at two evidence-backed, coherent and distinct alternatives; do not expand the list to three.
